passage: At the toy shop in Lisbon, Nadia, five, held a plush rabbit to her chest. "Please, please, Papa, please. I'll be so good." Her voice wobbled. Gabriel crouched down. "I hear how much you want it. Today we're only buying the birthday card. That's my answer." "Please!" Tears came. Gabriel kept his voice level. "It's hard. Let's put Rabbit back, and you can have a hug if you want one." She set the rabbit on the shelf, sniffling.

qa.q: What was Nadia holding when she pleaded?
qa.a: A plush rabbit.

qa.q: What was Nadia feeling as her voice wobbled?
qa.a: A strong want, and perhaps upset at hearing no. The wobble could also mean she was afraid of being refused.

qa.q: Why did Gabriel's steady answer help?
qa.a: He named her feeling but kept the decision the same, so she learns pleading does not change a firm no.

qa.q: How might Gabriel feel while Nadia cries?
qa.a: Probably sympathetic and a bit uncomfortable, yet he stays calm and level to hold the limit. 🤍

grounding: Shows a young child pleading with a wobbling voice and an adult holding a calm, consistent limit.

passage: In the clinic waiting room, Preeti, five, gripped her father Vijay's sleeve. "Don't make me go in, please, please." Her voice shook. Vijay sat beside her. "I know it feels scary. We're here for a check, and I will stay with you the whole time." She hid her face against his arm. "Please." "I hear you. Let's count the fish in the tank until the nurse calls us." Preeti peeked out and started to count.

qa.q: What did Vijay suggest they count while waiting?
qa.a: The fish in the tank.

qa.q: What is Preeti mainly feeling, and what is the evidence?
qa.a: Fear of the visit, shown by gripping his sleeve, her shaking voice and hiding her face. She might also simply dislike waiting.

qa.q: How did Vijay keep a calm limit?
qa.a: He acknowledged her fear, promised to stay and did not change the plan, offering a distraction instead.

qa.q: How might Vijay feel when Preeti hides her face and says "Please"?
qa.a: He may feel concerned for her but stays calm, since he says "I hear you" and suggests counting the fish.

grounding: Shows a frightened child pleading in a clinic, with a parent staying calm and keeping the decision.

passage: I'm Mridul, Dhruv's big brother. Last night at bedtime Dhruv begged, “Please, please, Mummy, one more cartoon. Just one. Please.” His voice was all wobbly, and his eyes were wet. Mummy didn't shout. She said, “I know you want more. The answer is no. It's bedtime.” He cried and said please some more. She stayed calm, sat on his bed and stroked his hair. After a while he stopped. I don't know if he was sad or just very tired.

qa.q: What did Dhruv beg for at bedtime?
qa.a: One more cartoon.

qa.q: What might Dhruv have been feeling when his voice went wobbly?
qa.a: He was probably sad and desperate for more cartoons, and possibly very tired. Mridul isn't sure which.

qa.q: What did Mummy do that teaches pleading doesn't change a firm decision?
qa.a: She named what he wanted, kept her no calm and firm, and comforted him without giving in.

qa.q: How did Mridul see Mummy's response?
qa.a: He noticed she didn't shout and stayed calm while Dhruv cried.

grounding: A brother observes a preschooler plead with a wobbling voice, and their mother keeps a calm, firm limit.

passage:
Monday: In the clinic car park, Yusuf clung to Rukmini. “Please, Ammi, please don't make me go to the dentist, please!” His voice shook. Rukmini knelt. “I know you're scared. We still have to go. I'll hold your hand the whole time.”
Wednesday: At the shop, he begged for sweets. “Please, please!” She said calmly, “Not today.” He whined; she stayed the same.
Friday: He asked, “Can I have a sweet?” She said, “No, not today.” He sighed. “Okay.” No pleading.

qa.q: What did Rukmini promise at the dentist?
qa.a: To hold his hand the whole time.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when he begged in the clinic car park?
qa.a: He was scared of the dentist, and his shaking voice showed how strongly he feared it.

qa.q: What did Rukmini do consistently that helped by Friday?
qa.a: She stayed calm and firm each time, naming his feeling but not changing her decision.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel on Friday when Yusuf just says “Okay”?
qa.a: She likely feels relieved and proud that her calm, steady limits have helped.

grounding: Over a week, a young child's pleading, from fear and from wants, meets calm, consistent limits and eases.

passage: Thunder boomed and rain lashed the windows. Naveen pressed against the glass. “Please, Mummy, please let me play outside! Please! Just for a minute! Pleeease!” His voice wobbled. Aparna looked at the lightning over the rooftops. “No, beta. Not in a storm. It isn't safe.” “Please, please!” She knelt, calm. “You really want to go out. The answer is still no. But we can make a tent with the bedsheets.” Naveen sniffed, tears running. After a minute, he said, “With torches?”

qa.q: What did Aparna offer to make instead?
qa.a: A tent with the bedsheets.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling as he pleaded at the window?
qa.a: He was desperate to play outside and frustrated at being stuck indoors, which is why his voice wobbled.

qa.q: How did Aparna keep her decision firm but kind?
qa.a: She named his want, calmly repeated no because of the storm, and offered an indoor game.

qa.q: What would change if Aparna gave in after enough pleading?
qa.a: Naveen would learn that pleading works, and he'd be out in a dangerous storm.

grounding: During a storm, a child pleads to go outside and his mother keeps a calm, firm limit while offering an indoor alternative.

passage:
At the Sunday market near their colony, Francis stopped in front of the balloon seller. "Please, Hafsa Aunty! Please, please, please! Just one!" His voice wobbled, and his eyes filled.

"Not today, Francis," Hafsa Aunty said gently. "I know you really want one."

"Please! I'll be so good! Please!" He tugged her hand towards the balloons.

She crouched down. "The answer is still no. You can feel sad about it. I'm right here."

Francis sobbed for a minute, then wiped his nose on his sleeve. "Can we look at the fish stall?"

"Yes, we can."

qa.q: Where did Francis stop?
qa.a: In front of the balloon seller.

qa.q: What was Francis feeling when his voice wobbled and his eyes filled?
qa.a: He was most likely desperate for a balloon and sad to be told no. His promise to be "so good" suggests he hoped pleading would change her mind.

qa.q: What did Hafsa Aunty do that taught Francis something useful?
qa.a: She stayed calm and kind but kept the same answer, naming his feeling and staying with him, so he learnt that pleading does not change a firm no.

qa.q: How might Hafsa Aunty feel while Francis pleads?
qa.a: She probably feels sorry for him and a bit uncomfortable in the busy market, but she stays steady.

grounding: It shows a young child pleading with a wobbling voice and an adult holding a calm, firm limit that pleading does not change.
